hints: Focus on how first ionisation energy changes down a group, and what second highest and third highest actually mean in terms of position.
Remember the top element has the highest value, so second highest means Period 3 and third highest means Period 4 for most main groups.
Check each pair, Ca and Cl, Mg and Br, K and S, to see if one is from Period 3 and the other is from Period 4.
walkthrough:
**Recall the group trend in ionisation energy**

First ionisation energy generally decreases down a group. This is because the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is easier to remove.

Trend down a group:
$$\text{ionisation energy decreases down the group}$$

**Translate second and third highest into periods**

The highest value is the top element of the group in Period 2. So second highest is the Period 3 element, and third highest is the Period 4 element.

That means we are looking for one Period 3 element joined to one Period 4 element.

**Test compound 1: calcium chloride**

Calcium is Group 2, Period 4. Its order is $\text{Be} > \text{Mg} > \text{Ca}$, so Ca is third highest. Chlorine is Group 17, Period 3. Its order is $\text{F} > \text{Cl} > \text{Br}$, so Cl is second highest.

$$\text{CaCl}_2: \text{Ca (3rd) + Cl (2nd) fits}$$

**Test compounds 2 and 3**

Magnesium is Group 2, Period 3, so second highest after Be. Bromine is Group 17, Period 4, so third highest after F and Cl. That fits.

Potassium is Group 1, Period 4. Its order is $\text{Li} > \text{Na} > \text{K}$, so K is third highest. Sulfur is Group 16, Period 3. Its order is $\text{O} > \text{S} > \text{Se}$, so S is second highest. That also fits.

$$\text{MgBr}_2: \text{Mg (2nd) + Br (3rd) fits}$$
$$\text{K}_2\text{S}: \text{K (3rd) + S (2nd) fits}$$

**Conclude the combination**

All three compounds are made from one Period 3 element and one Period 4 element, which is exactly one second highest plus one third highest. So 1, 2 and 3 are all possible.

options.A: Correct. All three fit the pattern. 1 has Cl (2nd in Group 17) with Ca (3rd in Group 2). 2 has Mg (2nd in Group 2) with Br (3rd in Group 17). 3 has S (2nd in Group 16) with K (3rd in Group 1).
options.B: Incorrect. This suggests only 1 and 2 work. Compound 3 also works because K is Period 4 (third after Li and Na) and S is Period 3 (second after O).
options.C: Incorrect. This leaves out compound 1. Calcium chloride does work because Ca is third in Group 2 and Cl is second in Group 17.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only compound 1 works. Both magnesium bromide and potassium sulfide also pair a Period 3 element with a Period 4 element, so they also satisfy the condition.
